data.outcome_summary: This IEA brief summarizes international trends in reading attitudes using PIRLS fourth-grade questionnaire data collected in 2001, 2006, 2011, and 2016. It constructs two attitude scales from questionnaire items that remained unchanged across cycles: students like reading (three items; 0–9 scale) and parents like reading (four items; 0–12 scale). For each country participating in all four cycles (18 countries) plus benchmarking participants (Ontario and Quebec), the brief computes average scale scores for each PIRLS year and conducts significance tests to assess whether country means changed over time. Results show widespread declines: students like reading decreased in most countries between 2001 and 2016, and parents like reading decreased in most countries between 2001 and 2016 as well. The analysis is descriptive and does not establish causal drivers; it also does not report detailed survey-weighting or missing-data procedures in the provided excerpt, limiting interpretability of the magnitude of change.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This record is a descriptive trend brief rather than an empirical machine-learning study: it reports country-level mean changes in questionnaire-based attitude scales across PIRLS cycles, with no ML model training, no predictive targets, and no reported PV-based scaling. Consequently, fields related to ML techniques and structured predictive findings are intentionally empty. The excerpt also does not provide student-level sample sizes or explicit weighting/missing-data procedures, which is consistent with a policy brief format focused on trend visualization and significance testing rather than full technical documentation.
